text: A risk score is useless without a threshold. This video plans how that threshold gets chosen -- before any model exists to apply it to.
Two ways to be wrong: miss a real at-risk account, or flag an account that never needed outreach. Those don't cost the same.
A missed account costs roughly its annual contract value. An unnecessary outreach costs maybe thirty minutes of a rep's time. The gap between those drives the threshold.
The plan: sweep candidate thresholds, pick the one that minimizes total expected cost, and report precision and recall side by side -- not one blended number.
Training and test data get a stratified split by account, so the comparison between models is fair. No numbers yet -- that's next, once a model actually exists.
